newsitem.title: CHINA: China finishes work on first joint venture railway.
newsitem.headline: China finishes work on first joint venture railway.

text.p: China's eastern Zhejiang province has finished laying track for the country's first joint venture railroad and expects the line to start full operation in the first half of next year, an official said on Friday.

The 251-km (156-mile) railroad linking Jinhua to Wenzhou was built with Hong Kong's Lin Ying Co and had total investment of 2.0 billion yuan ($241 million), an official from the joint venture company Zhejiang Jinwen Railway Development Co said.
China's Ministry of Railways held a 30 percent stake in the line, with Zhejiang Provincial Railway taking 45 percent and Lin Ying 25 percent, he said by telephone.
Zhejiang Jinwen would operate the railroad for 70 years, he said.
The railroad was expected to carry more than four million tonnes of goods and four million passengers a year, he said.
